correlation_feasibility.baseline_unit: Distinct event.id per explicitly defined cohort; installation, registry, process and sequence units are reported separately.
correlation_feasibility.confidence_value: Independent ancestry and service-object agreement add context; they do not prove maliciousness or a reduced false-positive rate.
correlation_feasibility.correlation_unit: Distinct ordered event-ID tuple; count participating baseline events separately from pair/sequence counts.
correlation_feasibility.false_negative_tradeoff: Missing process records, unmatched service object spelling, delayed/asynchronous execution or absent timestamps can remove otherwise relevant baseline events.
correlation_feasibility.primary_implementable_plan: A distinct service-origin cmd process followed by a PowerShell child using host plus process GUID; SCM imagePath provides an independently retrieved object confirmation.

global_limitations: Publisher/Wazuh annotations and scenarios are context only, never behavioural predicates.
All shortlisted observable cohorts have explicit UTC; the 11410 undated corpus events remain excluded from ordered correlation.
No independent malicious/benign truth supports precision, recall, F1 or FPR.
Historical event range is 2024-10-29 through 2024-12-22 UTC; no timestamp rewrite or wall-clock alert schedule is used.
Exploratory substring queries are cohort locators, not final detection syntax or tuned rules.
Windows escaping and HTML entities remain preserved; commands are inspected as text and never executed.

same_parent_justification: PowerShell and Windows Command Shell share T1059 but expose distinct argument, execution and ancestry behaviours. The selected Windows Service adds a different mechanism and two other tactics; observed independent events justify keeping both interpreters.

attack_guidance.absent: Native PowerShell provider logs, including 4103/4104/4105/4106 and 400/403, were not observed.
attack_guidance.present: Sysmon 1 process creation; Sysmon 7 module telemetry exists; other mapped supporting events can be explored.
attack_guidance.summary: Inspect interpreter arguments and ancestry together with module, network or child-process observations; direct and hosted PowerShell require different coverage.

selected.behaviour: Observed PowerShell process execution with command content and parent context; encoded arguments, remote retrieval/execution and unusual descendants warrant review. A PowerShell launch alone does not establish maliciousness.

car.name: Powershell Execution
car.use: Process creation and non-interactive parent context; an explorer-parent exclusion is a contextual concept, not copied as a final rule.

detection_plan.baseline: Inventory Sysmon process creations whose executable/name identifies PowerShell. Count distinct event IDs.
false_negative_concerns: Encoded variants not matched by a simple argument probe
false_positive_candidates: Process inventory command retained as a semantic comparison; its Public-directory splunkd.exe parent remains suspicious, so this is not clean benign evidence.
detection_plan.stronger: Evaluate argument structure, script retrieval/execution, parent context and independent child/file/network observations. Do not treat ExecutionPolicy Bypass alone as sufficient.
detection_plan.supporting_event: Join a separately observed child process by host and process GUID; optionally check files, modules or network records from the same process.

limitations: Counts describe observed launches, not confirmed attacks.
Native script contents and independent ground truth are unavailable.
selected.name: PowerShell
selected.rationale: Direct interpreter launches expose commands and ancestry. Encoded/bypass variants and observed child shells support a contextual analytic; routine process inventory provides a comparison candidate.

attack_guidance.absent: DET0552 lists Security 4697 and Sysmon 6/14; these are absent. SCM 7045 is the dataset substitution, not falsely described as 4697.
attack_guidance.present: Sysmon 1 and 13 are present. SCM System 7045 supplies service-installation evidence corresponding to the service creation concept.
attack_guidance.summary: Combine service creation/configuration, registry changes and process lineage; inspect unusual executable locations or service-launched interpreters.

selected.behaviour: A service is installed, or its executable configuration is changed. Command-line sc create/config, Services ImagePath modifications, and service-origin shell execution provide observable variants. Installation does not prove successful or lasting service execution.

car.name: Services launching Cmd
car.use: Direct service-origin shell behaviour, observed in three independent process records.

car.name: Service Outlier Executables
car.use: Service executable comparison; no 30-day clean baseline or copied historical pseudocode is claimed.

detection_plan.baseline: Inventory SCM 7045 installations; retain sc.exe creation and binPath modification as a separate process-event baseline with its own denominator.
false_negative_concerns: API or PowerShell service changes outside sc.exe
Service creation records missing from corpus
Service name/imagePath unindexed in current mapping
Successful persistence cannot be inferred from a creation command
false_positive_candidates: Approved service configuration or simulation tests
detection_plan.mapping_constraint: SCM serviceName/imagePath are preserved under literal keys in a disabled original object. They can be retrieved for review but cannot be used directly in indexed KQL/EQL joins. The currently implementable GUID pair uses ECS only; automating the third object join requires a separately reviewed extraction approach.
detection_plan.stronger: Assess service command/path choices, shell or PowerShell payloads, and independent registry/process observations; do not score a service name alone as malicious.
detection_plan.supporting_event: Correlate observed shell -> sc.exe by GUID. Investigate SCM installation -> services-origin shell by full image path plus host, then shell -> PowerShell by GUID.

limitations: The 102 installations and supporting telemetry are event cohorts, not counts of unique attacks.
Service object fields are retrieved evidence, currently unindexed.
Observed marker-file service tests admit an authorized simulation explanation.
selected.name: Windows Service
selected.rationale: SCM 7045 directly records installation with a service name and image path. Separate sc.exe creation/configuration and ImagePath registry events support additional behavioural probes and routine update comparisons.
